sources.excerpt: November 11, 2025 - The brain also remains active during rest, managing vital functions such

reasoning: The claim that humans only use 10% of their brain capacity is a widespread myth with no basis in neuroscience. Neuroimaging technologies such as fMRI and PET scans demonstrate that virtually all areas of the brain are active and serve dedicated functions, even during sleep or simple tasks. Furthermore, neurological research shows that unused brain tissue rapidly degenerates (atrophies), meaning that if 90% of the brain were truly dormant, massive brain damage would have little impact, which is demonstrably false. Reputable scientific and medical institutions, including MIT's McGovern Institute and Scientific American, unequivocally classify this notion as a scientific misconception.
